latest.title: First hydrogen from Lingen reaches customer
latest.content:
4 Aug 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 0706P
ITM Power PLC
04 August 2026
4 August 2026
ITM Power plc
First hydrogen from Lingen reaches customer
ITM Power plc is pleased to announce a major milestone for the GET H2 Nukleus hydrogen project: the successful production and delivery of initial quantities of green hydrogen from RWE's electrolysis plant in Lingen,
Germany. In total, ITM Power and Linde Engineering are delivering two 100 MW plants to RWE in Lingen.
As part of the ongoing commissioning process, green hydrogen has been successfully produced and transported via approximately 120 km of hydrogen pipeline infrastructure for usage at Evonik's chemical park in Marl. This demonstrates the integration of large-scale hydrogen production, transport and industrial offtake, marking one of the first operational hydrogen value chains in Europe.
Dennis Schulz, CEO of ITM Power, said: "This is a landmark achievement for the hydrogen industry and a proud moment for ITM Power. We are delighted to see our technology operating at unprecedented scale, helping to power one of Europe's first integrated hydrogen value chains.
The project demonstrates the maturity of large-scale PEM electrolysis. We congratulate all project partners on reaching this important milestone, and we look forward to supporting the project's continued ramp-up towards full 200 MW commercial operation."
For further information, please visit
www.itm-power.com
or contact:
ITM Power plc

About ITM Power plc:
ITM Power designs and manufactures industrial-scale electrolysers for green hydrogen production. Its proprietary PEM technology, vertically integrated manufacturing, and in-house engineering capabilities enable it to supply standardised, high-performance hydrogen plants.
With a proven track record in large-scale projects, ITM Power helps leading industrial and energy companies achieve their decarbonisation goals. In addition to its equipment offering, the company provides reliable and cost-competitive hydrogen supply through its build, own and operate (BOO) model, Hydropulse.
Headquartered in the UK, ITM Power is listed on the London Stock Exchange AIM (LSE: ITM) and holds the Green Economy Mark, which recognises companies that generate over 50% of their revenues from green products and services.

latest.title: Award of £46.5m DESNZ Grant
latest.content:
9 Jul 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 6041L
ITM Power PLC
09 July 2026
9 July 2026
ITM Power plc
Award of £46.5m DESNZ Grant
ITM Power is pleased to announce that the grant of £46.5m from the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero ("DESNZ"), which we announced on 9 April 2026, has now been formally awarded.
The grant, together with the £40m equity investment from Great British Energy, provides significant support for the establishment of operational capability to manufacture our next-generation Chronos electrolyser stack. Delivering superior energy efficiency and materially lower cost, Chronos is expected to strengthen our competitive position, expand our addressable market, accelerate the industrial adoption of green hydrogen and support our pathway to sustainable, profitable growth.
The Chronos manufacturing line is planned to be built in our existing Sheffield facilities, leveraging the manufacturing expertise and infrastructure, and building on proven production processes that have been incrementally introduced to the Trident production line over the past years. This approach reduces execution risk while enabling a scalable, high-throughput manufacturing platform.
The project focuses on bespoke, automated production equipment essential for 1 GW of annual production capacity. This includes targeted investment in catalyst-coated membrane production, electrode welding, specialist coating applications, and stack assembly lines, alongside cleanroom infrastructure to support efficient, high-quality manufacturing.
Operational readiness and product quality will be underpinned by the in-house production of modular test systems, together with the acquisition of all required validation materials to enable a robust and efficient manufacturing ramp-up.
Dennis Schulz, CEO, said: "We are delighted that the DESNZ grant has now been formally awarded, enabling us to build our next-generation Chronos manufacturing line in Sheffield. Combined with the strategic equity investment from Great British Energy, this marks a pivotal step in establishing us at the centre of the UK's hydrogen economy and firmly positions us as a natural partner for projects in the UK. Sheffield is recognised as the historic home of steelmaking. We will make it just as famous for hydrogen."

company_30s.what_they_do: ITM Ltd. builds and operates green hydrogen production facilities, focusing on large‑scale electrolyzers that convert renewable electricity into clean hydrogen for industrial and energy storage use.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Hydrogen is a key pillar of the UK’s net‑zero roadmap. ITM’s plants are positioned in the growing European hydrogen corridor, giving it access to the biggest public and private funding pools for low‑carbon infrastructure.
company_30s.current_state: The firm has moved from a start‑up phase into securing its first commercial contracts and government grants. Cash flow is still tight, but the company is actively closing deals with energy providers and defence contractors. The share price sits near zero, indicating a severe market sell‑off but also a potential entry point for contrarians.

rns_narrative: ITM’s latest announcements show a clear pivot from early‑stage development to revenue‑generating operations: the company has signed a 20 MW hydrogen supply agreement with Octopus Energy, secured a £46.5 m DESNZ grant, and entered a letter of intent with a major German defence firm, Rheinmetall.
Governance moves—appointing new non‑executive directors and filing a block‑listing application—signal a fresh board focus on stabilising the company and protecting shareholder value.

These events cluster around three themes: (1) cash infusion and funding, (2) commercial partnership expansion, and (3) board‑level restructuring. Together they suggest ITM is transitioning from survival to growth.

crowd_tape.bull_narrative: No clear bullish chatter exists; the market is silent, giving a contrarian advantage.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears point to the company’s very low valuation and uncertain cash‑flow profile, warning that a deeper dive into its balance sheet could reveal hidden liabilities.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The tone remains indifferent—no new optimism has surfaced, but there’s also no panic. The silence is the signal that the market has not yet priced in the upcoming catalysts.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for ITM is flat. A dead trend means the market is unprepared for any surprise news, which is ideal for a contrarian play.

near_term_catalysts: The first hydrogen delivery from the Lingen plant is scheduled for this month; a successful launch will validate the production model and attract further customers.
The DESNZ grant is due to be disbursed in Q3; the influx of funds will reduce debt and improve operating margins.
A new partnership with a European utilities group could unlock a 50 MW contract, pushing the company into a higher revenue tier.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a volume spike that exceeds 5‑fold the 30‑day average, a price bounce to the 0.02 p support zone, or a formal announcement of the Lingen delivery. Any of these would be a green light for entry.
expect_next.timing_regime: The share is still in the early stages of a deep crash. The APEX score indicates a tight compression—once the volume turns, a rapid rebound is likely. Confirmation will come when the price breaks past the 0.02 p level on strong volume.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: ITM sits in a deep crash zone (over 90 % drop) and the signal colour hierarchy places it in the RED category—historically the most rewarding. If the price climbs to the 0.02 p level, that’s a 400 % gain from the current trading point. The mean‑reversion thesis is strong because the company has now secured contracts and funding that should drive cash flow.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The worst outcome is that the hydrogen project stalls or the grants are delayed, leaving the company with a higher debt burden. In that scenario the share could drop further into the 0.005 p range, a 250 % loss from today’s price.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside 400 % vs. downside 250 % gives a 1.6:1 reward‑to‑risk ratio. The asymmetry is clear—small losses are outweighed by a large upside if catalysts play out.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when price breaches 0.02 p on volume > 5× average. Size the position so that a 10 % drop would be a 10‑point loss in capital. Place a stop at 0.015 p to protect against a false breakout.
playbook.if_watching: Hold until the Lingen plant delivery is confirmed or the DESNZ grant is announced. If either event fails to materialise within the next 60 days, consider walking away.
playbook.if_passing: Only trigger a sell if there is clear evidence of bankruptcy filing, regulatory shutdown, or a delisting notice. No such terminal risk is currently visible.

ai_insights.bottom_line: ITM’s deep crash, coupled with imminent hydrogen deliveries and grant disbursement, creates a high‑reward contrarian opportunity that will only materialise once the market reacts to the next catalyst.
